subject.title: [Bug]: Control UI header logo/icon not displaying after 2026.3.24 update

question: Should root-mounted Control UI support hard refreshes and bookmarks on arbitrary or legacy non-tab route prefixes with public assets resolving, or should support stay limited to documented root, known app routes, configured basePath, and the /__openclaw__ entrypoints?
rationale: Current source shows a remaining route-prefix public-asset gap, but fixing it changes the supported URL contract and static-file routing boundary; automation should not choose that product/security boundary while an open fork PR proposes a conflicting fix shape.

options.title: Support Safe Prefixed Public Assets
options.body: Land a narrow allowlist for known Control UI public assets under supported SPA prefixes, preserve 404/fallthrough for unknown static paths and non-read methods, and close or replace the fork PR after proof.

options.title: Limit To Documented Entrypoints
options.body: Declare arbitrary or legacy non-tab prefixes unsupported, document root/configured-basePath entrypoints, and close this issue plus the fork PR with that rationale.

options.title: Adopt The Fork Direction
options.body: Review the open fork PR as the implementation candidate only if its asset, CSP, and route-boundary behavior matches the chosen contract; otherwise request a fresh narrow PR.

recommendation.title: Support Safe Prefixed Public Assets
recommendation.body: Land a narrow allowlist for known Control UI public assets under supported SPA prefixes, preserve 404/fallthrough for unknown static paths and non-read methods, and close or replace the fork PR after proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent gateway public-asset and Control UI static-serving history is the strongest evidence-backed owner signal for deciding the URL routing boundary.
